title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
claim: Our method reaches higher scores with far fewer samples than a reinforcement-learning baseline and a leading competitor, and the gain holds on held-out data.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, left-to-right, star markers for held-out test results
description: Two side-by-side line charts, (a) HotpotQA and (b) IFBench, both with Qwen3 8B. The x-axis is the number of rollouts, from 0 to 25,000. The y-axis is score. Each chart has four colored series: gray for the baseline, green for MIPROv2, orange for GRPO and blue for GEPA. Dots mark validation performance. Star markers mark test-set performance. The blue GEPA curve jumps up within the first few hundred rollouts and plateaus well above the others. The green MIPROv2 curve also rises early but plateaus lower. The orange GRPO curve climbs slowly in steps over 24,000 rollouts and ends lower. A legend box sits at the top right of each chart. Panel (b) has a second y-axis on the right for test-set score. A blue star sits highest in each chart, so the eye goes to the top-left corner.
caption: A comparison of learning behavior of the GEPA prompt optimizer against a state-of-the-art prompt optimizer (MIPROv2) and GRPO (24,000 rollouts). As more rollouts are sampled, the prompt optimizers can learn much more quickly than GRPO. GEPA substantially outperforms both GRPO and MIPROv2 in final score. The Test-set star markers demonstrate the performance gap in a held-out set of questions.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly adapted to downstream tasks via reinforcement learning (RL) methods like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), which often require thousands of rollouts to learn new tasks. We argue that the interpretable nature of language often provides a much richer learning medium for LLMs, compared to policy gradients derived from sparse, scalar rewards. To test this, we introduce GEPA (Genetic-Pareto), a prompt optimizer that thoroughly incorporates natural language reflection to learn high-level rules from trial and error. Given any AI system containing one or more LLM prompts, GEPA samples trajectories (e.g., reasoning, tool calls, and tool outputs) and reflects on them in natural language to diagnose problems, propose and test prompt updates, and combine complementary lessons from the Pareto frontier of its own attempts. As a result of GEPA's design, it can often turn even just a few rollouts into a large quality gain. Across six tasks, GEPA outperforms GRPO by 6% on average and by up to 20%, while using up to 35x fewer rollouts. GEPA also outperforms the leading prompt optimizer, MIPROv2, by over 10% (e.g., +12% accuracy on AIME-2025), and demonstrates promising results as an inference-time search strategy for code optimization. We release our code at https://github.com/gepa-ai/gepa .
